summary: George M. Reith, the Presbyterian minister in Singapore, wrote these letters to the Singapore Free Press during a holiday tour that began in February 1896, and they were reprinted as a book the next year. He went by small steamer to Sourabaya, Bali, and Lombok soon after the fighting of 1894, Macassar in Celebes, and Sumbawa; then through Java, to the crater of the Bromo, Jokjakarta, the temples of Boro Boedoer and Parambanan, Garoet, Buitenzorg, and Batavia; and last to Bangkok and Ayuthia in Siam. He writes in the first person and with humour of fellow passengers, Dutch officials and colonial manners, the Dutch language, native rulers and markets, temples and volcanoes, and of what the journey cost. Malay words are translated in footnotes.
